# Part 377 — Payment of Transportation Charges
## Overview
Under Part 377, carriers that offer COD service must publish tariff rules governing that service. The regulation sets a 15-day deadline for remitting COD collections to the consignor or payee after delivery of the shipment. Carriers that choose not to publish their own COD tariff must instead remit collections directly within that 15-day window without deduction.
## Key Provisions
Governs carriers that handle cash-on-delivery (COD) freight shipments in interstate commerce.

Requires carriers offering COD service to publish tariff rules governing the service.

Sets a 15-day deadline for remitting COD collections to the consignor after delivery.

Does not apply to transportation on railroad bills of lading or freight forwarder billing.

Applies to for-hire carriers of property subject to 49 U.S.C. 13702.
### How quickly must a carrier remit COD funds?
Under Part 377, carriers must remit COD collections to the consignor or payee within 15 days after delivery of the shipment. If the carrier has published a COD tariff allowing a different arrangement, those tariff terms govern, but the 15-day default applies otherwise.

linkup.title: Collect on Delivery C.o.d. Obligations — Law of Wrongdoing — American Legal Digest
linkup.snippet:
Under 49 C.F.R. § 377.105, a carrier that chooses to provide C.O.D. service may either publish and maintain a tariff setting forth nondiscriminatory rules governing C.O.D. service or, in lieu of such a tariff, adopt a rule requiring remittance of each C.O.D. collection directly to the consignor or designated payee within fifteen days of delivery ([49 C.F.R. § 377.105](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-1999-title49-vol4/pdf/CFR-1999-title49-vol4-subtitleB-chapIII.pdf)).
### Default Rule: Direct Remittance Within Fifteen Days  
A motor common carrier that provides C.O.D. service today has two regulatory pathways. Under the default rule, the carrier adopts a tariff provision requiring direct remittance of each C.O.D. collection to the consignor or designated payee within fifteen days after delivery to the consignee ([49 C.F.R. § 377.105](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-1999-title49-vol4/pdf/CFR-1999-title49-vol4-subtitleB-chapIII.pdf)). The fifteen-day clock runs from delivery to the consignee, not from collection; collection is presumed to occur contemporaneously with delivery in a properly performed C.O.D. transaction. Failure to remit within fifteen days is a regulatory violation exposing the carrier to administrative sanction.
The C.O.D. obligation of a common carrier is doctrinally unitary: a fiduciary-grade duty to collect, hold, and remit money on behalf of the consignor, enforceable at common law as a breach of agency and bailment and at federal regulatory law as a violation of the tariff-filing, remittance, and reporting requirements of 49 C.F.R. Parts 373, 375, and 377.
The regulatory regime adds administrative specificity - fifteen-day default remittance, mandatory tariff publication, household-goods annual performance reporting, freight-forwarder receipt obligations - that the common-law regime could not provide, and the household-goods reporting regime adds a service-quality transparency layer that operates alongside the older fiduciary-duty

Title 58 - Public Utilities, Services and Carriers

Section 58-13-450. Returns and remittances on C. O. D. shipments.
                                            All common carriers doing business in this State and making collections on C. O. D. shipments for shippers or other persons designated by the shipper shall pay over to such shipper or person designated by such shipper the returns or moneys collected on C. O. D. shipments within fifteen days after the date of such collection from the consignee. D. collection and in addition thereto a penalty of twenty-five dollars, to be recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction, either in the same suit on the claim or in a separate action.

ultimate.snippet: Every motor carrier of property subject to [49 U.S.C. 13702](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/49/13702), except as otherwise provided in [§ 377.101](/current/title-49/section-377.101), which chooses to provide c.o.d. service may publish and maintain, or cause to be published and maintained for its account, a tariff or tariffs which set forth nondiscriminatory rules governing c.o.d. service and the collection and remittance of c.o.d. funds. ultimate.snippet:
#### § 377.105 Collection and remittance.
Every motor carrier of property subject to 49 U.S.C. 13702, except as otherwise provided in § 377.101, which chooses to provide c.o.d. service may publish and maintain, or cause to be published and maintained for its account, a tariff or tariffs which set forth nondiscriminatory rules governing c.o.d. service and the collection and remittance of c.o.d. funds. Alternatively, any carrier that provides c.o.d. service, but does not wish to publish and maintain, or cause to be published and maintained, its own nondiscriminatory tariff, may adopt a rule requiring remittance of each c.o.d. collection directly to the consignor or other person designated by the consignor as payee within fifteen (15) days after delivery of the c.o.d. shipment to the consignee.

(c) *Length of credit period.* Unless a different credit period has been established by tariff publication pursuant to paragraph (d) of this section, the credit period is 15 days. It includes Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays.
